assessment.governing_intent: Identify the existing Python profile/transport revision, its custody and its configured scoped resources under its existing execution authority. Then, under the narrowly granted live-proof authority, prove a Python-only (no-Node) runtime baseline on the production path. The proof must cover instrumented no-Node process and dependency paths, real ingress, effect dispatch, durable consumer outcome and readback, and restart with readback. The purpose is to discharge the canonical_live_transport and node_independent_runtime_baseline prerequisite capabilities without inserting new requirements, repairing other owners' implementations, or releasing anything.
implementation_unknowns: Which exact Python profile/transport revision, custody record and configured scoped resources currently exist and are under existing execution authority. This is the first identification step the predicate requires.
How to instrument process and dependency paths so the absence of Node is demonstrated rather than assumed, for example process-tree and dependency tracing with a negative control.
How to pin FX-E1 executable commands, inputs, expected outcomes and evidence schema before implementation. This includes showing that the harness can tell intact, faulted and restored states apart.

How to exercise the one-writer guard during the proof so that Node dispatch of the same work is demonstrably excluded while Python runs, without disturbing protected Node/bootstrap operation (KEEP_UNTIL_REPLACED).
Which durable consumer readback surface and restart procedure on the production path produce immutable observation references the independent verifier can inspect.
Whether any candidate code change is needed at all (for example instrumentation or evidence tooling) versus a pure proof-and-evidence candidate. Custody still requires a published branch and SHA.
independent_decision_centers: Identify and prove the existing Python-only live transport baseline on the authorized production path. This is a single cohesive center: identification precedes and feeds the proof, and neither is meaningfully accepted or rejected alone.
material_risks: The authority grant was relayed by a Founder-authorized observing session, not by the Factory Director. The execution gate should confirm the handoff record's provenance before live calls, because this gate cannot verify it.
Predecessor DONE status is reported, not independently verified here. A source revision mismatch at execution time must hold the work.

The existing Python transport may turn out to be incomplete. Per the fixed decisions, work then returns to the existing requirement owner and holds; it is not repaired here. This could stall the BIU after live preparation has begun.

Real effect dispatch on the production path carries external side effects. It must stay within existing scoped resources and execution authority, keep checkpoint/rollback compatible, and never overlap Node dispatch of the same work.
Absence of Node could be asserted without discriminating instrumentation. Weak negative controls would make the no-Node claim unverifiable.
Budget is not explicitly bound in the text (tokens/cost are UNKNOWN when not exposed). An unbound budget or custody is a stated stop condition that the execution gate must clear.
A successful proof could be mistaken for release or operational authorization. The separate future Wave 2 operational-release grant remains required.
assessment.next_action:
Hand off to the execution queue as READY for the PRODUCER (Morty), with the following conditions at the execution gate:
1. Confirm the provenance of handoff founder-live-transport-proof-authority-20260926T070519Z.
2. Confirm budget and custody binding.
3. Before any live call, pin the FX-E1 fixture commands, evidence schema and intact/fault/restored discrimination.
4. Record the identified Python profile/transport revision, custody and scoped resources.
5. Only then execute the authorized live proof and publish the candidate SHA for JC's independent verification.
assessment.rationale: The controlling condition is that the prior HOLD's missing prerequisites (predecessor completion and an authorized operational target) are reported as resolved by a durable, narrowly scoped Founder decision. With those resolved, no owner intent remains ambiguous. Scope, non-goals, failure routing, the one-writer constraint and the release separation are explicitly fixed. The remaining uncertainty is engineering: identifying the existing transport, instrumenting no-Node paths, and designing evidence. That belongs in implementation_unknowns, not owner questions. The work forms one cohesive decision center with observable acceptance and a single meaningful independent verdict, so SPLIT is not warranted. HOLD is not warranted because no named prerequisite is stated to be unavailable. Authority provenance and budget binding are execution-gate checks already covered by the BIU's own stop conditions, not unresolved preconditions of this plan. READY recommends handoff only; it does not authorize IMPLEMENT, live operation or release.
assessment.summary: This revision answers the two conditions the prior HOLD named, as reported in the text. First, the three predecessors (WO-220501, WO-220403, WO-220103) are stated as DONE. Second, a Founder EXPLICIT_LIVE_TRANSPORT_PROOF_AUTHORITY grant is recorded (handoff founder-live-transport-proof-authority-20260926T070519Z). It names the existing, identified production-path Python profile/transport as the authorized operational target, which settles the earlier question of what can discharge acceptance beyond the local FX-E1 fixture. The grant is scoped to this BIU's live proof. It excludes release, cutover, Node/bootstrap retirement, sibling scope and broader production mutation. The work has one cohesive decision center: identify the existing Python transport, then prove it live end-to-end with readback and restart. Several behaviours are fixed rather than left open: missing implementation returns to its owner, invalid scope or missing readback holds, and simultaneous Node/Python dispatch is forbidden. No material owner intent remains open. These facts are reported by the task text; this gate has not verified them.
